description:
Parent: fz-kdt

## Goal

Keep a permanent corpus witness for the termination backstop that remains after
fz-kdt.106: a program whose publisher correlation is genuinely wider than
`ACTIVATION_INPUT_ROW_BUDGET`, causes budget widening, and propagates enough wide
evidence downstream to exercise a collapse cascade.

Guard the compile by machine-independent work counts. Do not use wall-clock
limits as a performance assertion.

## Current state

fz-kdt.106 removed collapse caused by ascent history. The four landed lenses now
assert exactly zero `fz.compiler2.activation_inputs.budget_collapsed` events.
That is the schedule-confluence gate for ordinary corpus programs, but it cannot
regress the still-reachable genuine-width path or its downstream work cost.

The classification rule is already recorded in
`backend_inventory_width_stays_pinned_on_the_target_fixtures`: emitted
executables may rise when, and only when, the same fixture demonstrates fewer
budget collapses because precise correlated rows replaced collapse-widened
sharing. Do not duplicate that deliverable here.

The review scratchpad `kdt106-review-stress1.fz` is not in the repository. Its
historical 588-executable/3-collapse result was measured near the fz-kdt.106
landing, before later specialization changes, and is not a valid current-main
pin until the exact source is recovered or reconstructed and remeasured.

## Strategy

1. Recover or reconstruct the small stress shape described by the review:
   fourteen independently typed element families, each passed through a
   distinct lambda to `Enum.all?/2`. Minimize it while preserving genuine
   correlation width and downstream collapse propagation.
2. Add it as a normal persistent behavior fixture, including checked stdout and
   the normal interp/JIT/AOT oracle coverage.
3. Drive that exact source through the public telemetry path on
   a3a9761d1209165e5230625b9347cf6b0ad09b83 before writing expected constants.
4. Add an exact work ratchet beside the public-trace work tests. Pin:
   - summed `activation_inputs.budget_collapsed` collapses;
   - backend/native executable inventory;
   - total formula evaluations;
   - total product settlements;
   - `AnalyzeActivation` evaluations and unchanged completions, so added work
     cannot hide behind an unchanged headline total.
5. Record the measured values and recipe in the test commentary. Re-pin only
   with a named semantic cause. Do not assert `time_ns`, elapsed duration, or a
   fixture timeout as performance evidence.
6. If the reconstructed fixture no longer produces a collapse on current main,
   do not bless zero or preserve the historical numbers. Minimize a new
   genuine-width witness first; if no reachable source can trigger the
   backstop, stop and reclassify the backstop/reachability premise.

## Red-first tests

- The new fixture emits at least one nonzero
  `fz.compiler2.activation_inputs.budget_collapsed` event on current main.
- The fixture reaches a settled backend/native program and has identical
  observable output through interp, JIT, and AOT.
- A public-trace test fails when any pinned work column or executable inventory
  moves.
- The existing four-lens zero-collapse test remains green, proving the new
  fixture is deliberate exceptional width rather than a regression in the
  ordinary corpus.

## Acceptance

- The stress source and expected output are durable repository files; no
  scratchpad dependency remains.
- Exact current-main values replace, rather than assume, the historical
  `588 executables / 3 collapses` observation.
- Collapse count and settlement/evaluation work are enforced from public
  telemetry only.
- Existing zero-collapse, public-trace causality, inventory, CLI, and fixture
  gates remain green.
- Documentation explains that the budget is a termination backstop, ordinary
  corpus programs are expected to remain at zero, and this fixture deliberately
  witnesses genuine correlation width.
title: Persist a genuine-width collapse cascade and pin its machine-independent compile work
